question.worked_solution:
The "square of a difference" formula states that

$$
{p}^{2}-2ap+{a}^{2}=(p-a)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
{p}^{2}-\frac{3}{2}p+\frac{9}{16}.
$$

First, we write the constant term as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{2}-\frac{3}{2}p+{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{2}-2\cdot \frac{3}{4}p+{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of difference formula with $a=\frac{3}{4}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{(p-\frac{3}{4})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
